notes: Serving Begins with the Holy Spirit
The First Station on the Path of Serving: Spirit
“The mind of the Spirit is life and peace”
Romans 8:6
• This lesson is the first station on the 321 Path of Serving: Spirit — the Holy Spirit is my guide.
• Announce the lesson title and subtitle, then invite the brothers and sisters to quieten their hearts.
• Three theme scriptures: Acts 1:8, Galatians 5:25, Romans 8:6.
• Three key words for the lesson: starting point, source, minding the Spirit.
Serving doesn’t start with ability
“What can I do?” is the wrong starting point
Serving doesn’t begin with “I can”
Serving begins with “the Holy Spirit”
Without the Spirit, there is no true serving
• Opening illustration: a sister who had served for seventeen years said, “I feel like a dishcloth that’s been wrung dry.”
• Ask: when you hear the word “serving”, what is the first sentence in your heart?
• Point out that most people first ask, “What can I do?”, but the Bible gives a completely different starting point.
• Quote Luke 3:21–22: Jesus was baptised, the Holy Spirit descended, and only then did he begin to serve.
• Zechariah 4:6: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.”
Theme Scriptures and Background
“Let’s also walk by the Spirit” Galatians 5:25
Acts: “the Acts of the Holy Spirit”
The Galatians’ mistake: begun in the Spirit
but completed in the flesh
• Acts was written by Luke the physician; with Luke’s Gospel it forms a two-volume work addressed to Theophilus.
• Acts 1:8 is the Lord’s last word before the ascension and the key to the whole book: first power, then witness.
• Galatians was written around AD 49; Galatians 3:3 exposes the error of “begun in the Spirit, completed in the flesh”.
• “Spirit” appears about twenty times in Romans 8 — the chapter with the greatest density of the Spirit in the whole Bible.
• Word note: ruach and pneuma both mean wind, breath and spirit (John 3:8).
Jesus’ Example: Beginning with the Spirit
Baptism, the Spirit comes, led, then serving
“Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit” Luke 4:1
“In the power of the Spirit” Luke 4:14
Not serving first, then the Spirit
• The first of the Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model — so look first at the Lord’s own order.
• Luke 4:18: in the Lord’s first sermon, the very first sentence is “The Spirit of the Lord is on me.”
• Stress the order: not serving first and then the Spirit, but the Spirit first and then serving.
• Ask: do we act first, or receive first?
Life First, Then Ministry
The Spirit first led Jesus into the wilderness
The Spirit doesn’t only lead us into work
The Spirit also shapes our life
321: life first, then relationships, then ministry
• The three temptations of the forty days — gain, reputation, power — are exactly where servants most easily fall.
• Picture: a thirty-storey tower needs a foundation over twenty metres deep; however high above ground, that deep below.

• Data: Freudenberger coined “burnout” in 1974; Maslach and Jackson put forward a three-dimension scale in 1981; the WHO included it in the eleventh revision of the International Classification of Diseases in 2019.
• Exodus 3:2: the bush burned with fire yet was not consumed, because the fire did not come from the bush.
• 321 application: life first, then relationships, then ministry.
The Apostles: Filled with the Spirit
They didn’t rush to act; they waited first
“You will receive power” Acts 1:8
Filled with the Spirit at Pentecost
One message, three thousand baptised
• Acts 1:4: Don’t depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father.
• “Wait” is perimenō: to wait around and not go away. A hundred and twenty waited ten days.
• “Power” is dynamis, the root of “dynamic” and “dynamite”.
• Acts 2:4 and 2:41: all were filled with the Spirit; about three thousand were added that day.
• Contrast: fifty days earlier Peter dared not acknowledge the Lord before a servant girl; fifty days later he preached boldly to thousands.
Begun by the Spirit, continued by the Spirit
Not Peter’s eloquence, but the Holy Spirit
“If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit”
Galatians 5:25
Not only at the beginning, but every day
• “Walk” is stoicheō: to advance in a line, to keep in step with the Spirit.
• Ephesians 5:18 “be filled with the Spirit” is present tense, passive voice, imperative mood: keep on being filled.
• Picture: your phone needs charging every day; you don’t skip today because you charged it yesterday.
• Science illustration: the Dead Sea is about 34 per cent salt, nearly ten times seawater; taking in without giving out means no life.
• 321 application: the 920 practice and 235 relationships; the ninefold fruit of Galatians 5:22–23.
Two Roads: the Flesh or the Spirit
“The mind of the flesh is death”
“The mind of the Spirit is life and peace”
Romans 8:6
Minding the flesh: relying on self, my own way
• “Mind” is phroneō: the settled orientation of one’s thinking, what one has on one’s mind.
• Romans 8:5: those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; those who live according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
• The flesh is not the body, but the old self’s nature that doesn’t rely on God and puts itself at the centre.
• Result: the more you serve, the more tired and dry you become, until you want to give up.
• In 321 language: the old self is self-centred; pride provokes pride, and both sides lose.
Heart and Spirit, Not Brain and Self
Weary from serving? The source is wrong
“But he who does the will of my Father”
Matthew 7:21
Rely on the heart: glad; on the brain: troubled
• Matthew 7:21–23: prophesying, casting out demons, mighty works — yet the Lord says, “I never knew you.”
• The point is not how much was done, but whether it came from God and whether there is a real relationship with the Lord.
• Colossians 3:15: let the peace of God rule in your hearts; “rule” originally meant the umpire at the games.
• Psychology: Deci and Ryan’s Self-Determination Theory — autonomous motivation lasts longer than controlled motivation.
• Isaiah 30:15: your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.
Five Daily Practices
Be filled with the Spirit first every day
Pause and seek before deciding
Discern the two voices; choose the Spirit
Don’t rely on self; 5. Examine before bed
• Practice 1: Luke 11:13 — how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?
• Practice 2: Acts 16:6–7 — forbidden by the Holy Spirit, not allowed by the Spirit; Paul paused.
• Practice 3: James 3:17 as the standard; rebuke brings repentance, accusation brings despair.
• Practice 4: Isaiah 40:31 — those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength.
• Practice 5: before bed ask, “Today, did I rely on the Holy Spirit, or on myself?”; deepen each through the eight stages.
From “I Do It” to “God Does It”
It isn’t you striving to serve
It’s the Spirit at work within you
From forcing it to flowing
Let Jesus be King; all glory to him
• Gentle reminder: the problem is never the tasks, but the source. With the Spirit as source there is life; with the flesh, only draining.
• Luke 10:41–42: the Lord didn’t rebuke Martha for serving, but for being anxious and troubled.
• John 15:5: the branch’s job is to stay joined to the vine; fruit is the natural result of the connection.
• Three-point call: let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory, go back to the first station today.
Prayer of Response and Blessing
Lord, my life begins with the Holy Spirit
I will no longer rely on myself
I choose to mind the Spirit
Let your Spirit fill me and use me
• Lead the brothers and sisters in the lesson’s declaration of faith together.
• Prayer: confess self-confidence and haste, ask for the Spirit’s filling, for a discerning heart, for life and peace.
• Blessing: may the Lord’s Spirit fill, guide and use every brother and sister.
• Close by giving all the glory to Jesus.
