blog.title: From Knowing into Living It Out

blocks.x: Is your service a firework, or a charcoal fire?
The night sky on Lunar New Year’s Eve. A firework shoots upward — bang! — and the whole sky bursts into golden flowers, while tens of thousands of people below look up at once and gasp.
Three seconds later, the light has scattered, the smoke has thinned, and the sky is pitch black again, as though nothing had ever happened.

The mouth of the stove in an old family home out in the countryside. A lump of charcoal, glowing quietly red. It doesn’t dazzle anyone, it draws no gasps, and it will never make it into a single photograph. Yet slowly the pot of water comes to the boil, slowly the whole room full of people grows warm — and when you brush aside the ash at dawn, it is still glowing red.
I often wonder which kind our service is.

A special conference: tears flow, the prayer is so fervent it seems about to lift the roof off, and everyone says, “This time it’s different!” Three months later the people have disappeared; six months later, no one can even remember what moved them in the first place.

On the other hand, there was a sister who, for twenty years without a break, came to church an hour early every Lord’s Day to boil the water and straighten the chairs. She couldn’t preach; her testimony was over in three minutes. Yet half the people in that church, in the very hardest stretch of their lives, were held up by a bowl of noodles she had cooked.
Where is the difference?
What we lack is not being moved, but “Life”
Many people have been moved, have received revelation, and love the Lord dearly. So why doesn’t their influence last?
Because one word is missing — Life.
James puts it very bluntly: “Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.” (James 2:17)
“Dead” in the original is the “dead” of a corpse. A corpse is not without form. A corpse has hands and feet and a face, everything there — except one thing: there is no breath.
A faith that has been stirred and has knowledge, yet never comes to be lived out, looks just like that in God’s eyes — everything complete, except that it doesn’t move.
The Lord Jesus said, “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.” (Matthew 7:24)
He didn’t say “everyone who hears these words of mine and understands them”, nor “and is moved by them”. He said, “and does them”.

Two verses later, the one who doesn’t do them is like a foolish man who built his house on the sand. Please note: the two men heard the same sermon. The difference wasn’t in the hearing; the difference was in the doing.

You have a cookbook at home. You’ve read it three times and can recite every dish. Are you full? No. To be fed, you have to walk into the kitchen, wash the rice, light the stove and put up with the smoke.
Reading the cookbook is comfortable; cooking is a bother. But only cooking can feed anyone.
Change is “gradual”, not instant
Someone says: I’ve tried. I really did try to live it out, and I failed.
Paul says the new self is “being renewed in knowledge” — gradually renewed (Colossians 3:10). In the original it is a present passive participle: continually being renewed.

In the old days, when a bolt of white cloth was to be dyed blue, a quick soak wasn’t enough. It went into the vat, out to dry — back into the vat, out to dry again — dipped again and again. Each time it looked only a shade darker, but after thirty times that cloth was blue through and through, and no washing could get it out.
Research by Phillippa Lally of University College London and her colleagues, published in 2010, found that it takes on average sixty-six days for a new behaviour to become an automatic habit.
Sixty-six days. Not six hours.
So please don’t give up because you fall on the third day. Falling isn’t the end; giving up is.
What has the most influence is not eloquence but life
Jesus’ service was not just preaching. He lived it before our eyes, and he died it before our eyes.

Yet John 6 records a chilling line: the crowds who wanted to crown him king yesterday turned away today over one saying that was hard to live — “At this, many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.”
The same miracle, the same preaching, the same Jesus. Those who left had come to get something; those who stayed were ready to hand over their whole lives.

Inside Biosphere 2 in Arizona, the trees grew fast and tall, yet toppled over one after another before they reached maturity. One reason was that inside that glasshouse there was no wind. Trees in the natural world stand firm precisely because they are buffeted by wind year after year, and so grow strengthened tissue and drive their roots deeper.
A tree that has never faced the wind grows fast but cannot stand.

Being moved and having knowledge is growing upward; having life is putting down roots. The part that grows upward everyone can see; the part that goes down only God can see — yet what decides whether a tree will stand is precisely the part no one sees.
Paul told the Thessalonians that he was pleased to give them not only the Good News, but his own soul as well.
The Good News is a message; our souls are our life. To give only the message is to pass on the word; to give your life along with it — that is to pass on life.
So: pass on life by life; let life influence life.
It isn’t you who influences people; it is the life of Christ influencing people through you.
This is the deepest power of service: living out Jesus with our lives.
Today’s reflection

→ Is there a word of God you have “heard” for a long time but never “done”? What is stopping you — inconvenience, the cost, or an unwilling heart? Today, choose that one word and find one concrete thing to do that puts it into action.

Preview the three points: living the truth out, renewal from the inside out, passing on life by life.

text: A firework, or a charcoal fire?
Firework: a three-second gasp
Charcoal: a whole night’s warmth
Which kind is your service?
notes: First picture: New Year’s Eve fireworks fill the sky with gold; three seconds later it is pitch black again.
Second picture: a lump of charcoal in a country stove, glowing quietly; brush the ash aside at dawn and it is still red.
Ask: is our service a firework, or a charcoal fire?
You may use the example of people gone three months after a conference, contrasted with the sister faithful for twenty years.

text: One word is missing: Life
Moved, given revelation, loving the Lord
yet the influence doesn’t last
Spirit and Understanding, but not lived out
The Path of Serving: Spirit → Understanding → Life
notes: Raise the lesson’s question: many are moved, receive revelation and love the Lord, yet their influence doesn’t last.
The reason: Spirit and Understanding but no action — faith stuck in the head and the feelings.
Explain why Understanding to Life is hardest: receiving costs nothing; living it out always costs something.
Hearing a sermon takes an hour; living out one sentence of it may take a lifetime.
Bring out the order of the Path of Serving: Spirit, Understanding, Life.

text: Theme verses and background
“The words that I speak to you
are spirit, and are life” John 6:63
James: true faith is always visible
John 6: many went back
notes: Read the full verse, John 6:63; “life” is zōē, God’s eternal life.

text: 1. From Revelation to Life
Many people stop here:
Hear → be moved → the end
God’s intention is:
Hear → understand → do → life
notes: Point out most people’s pattern: hear, be moved, the end — moved fifty-two times a year, life unchanged.
God’s intention has four steps: hear, understand, do, and so it becomes life.
Use the everyday scene of being moved in the morning and evaporated by afternoon, so listeners recognise themselves.

text: The wise man and the foolish man
“Everyone who hears these words of mine, and does them,
is like a wise man” Matthew 7:24
Both heard the same sermon
The difference isn’t hearing but doing
notes: Read the full verse, Matthew 7:24; “wise” is phronimos — someone with foresight.
Note that the Lord didn’t say “and understands them” or “and is moved by them”, but “and does them”.
Compare the foolish man of 7:26: both heard the same sermon; the difference lies in doing, not hearing.
Optionally add Luke 6:46: why do you call me “Lord, Lord”, and don’t do the things which I say?

text: Reading a cookbook won’t fill you
A perfect written test won’t drive the car
“Be doers of the word, and not only hearers,
deluding your own selves” James 1:22
Stanford research: the knowing-doing gap
notes: Picture: reading a cookbook three times won’t fill you; you must go into the kitchen, wash the rice and light the stove.

Read James 1:22; stress “deluding your own selves” — the greatest danger is fooling yourself.
Cite Pfeffer and Sutton of Stanford, The Knowing-Doing Gap (1999): talking about it is not doing it.
Optionally add Festinger’s 1957 theory of cognitive dissonance and the 1959 experiment: people often lower the standard to fit their behaviour.

text: 321: Implementation is the door
Eight stages: Information, Revelation,
Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction,
Repetition, Multiplication
God is waiting for an old obedience
notes: List all eight stages of changing our mindset; Information comes before Understanding, Revelation belongs to Understanding, and Implementation is where Life begins.
Note that many people spend their whole lives circling the first three stages and never take the fourth step.

Encourage choosing one sentence today and finding one concrete thing to do.

text: 2. God’s Word Restores the Soul
“Yahweh’s law is perfect,
restoring the soul” Psalm 19:7
Original: bringing the soul back to its position
Humility is returning to our originally intended position
notes: Read the full verse, Psalm 19:7; “restoring the soul” is literally “bringing back the soul”.
The root shuv means to turn back, to return; God’s word leads the wandering soul back to its originally intended position.
321: humility is returning to our originally intended position — let man be man and let God be God; pride is leaving it and wanting to take God’s place.
Stress that God’s word is not a burden but the road that leads the runaway heart back to the Father’s house.

text: Transformed by the renewing of your mind
“Don’t be conformed to this world,
but be transformed by the renewing of your mind” Romans 12:2
Conformed: the outward pattern
Transformed: the inner essence
notes: Read the full verse, Romans 12:2.
“Conformed” comes from schēma, the outward pattern, like the cut of a garment changing with fashion.
“Transformed” is metamorphoō — the word for Jesus’ transfiguration in Matthew 17:2 — a change of essence.
The original is a present passive imperative: you don’t transform yourself; you let God keep transforming you.
Optionally add 2 Corinthians 3:18: with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord, we are transformed into the same image.

text: Gradual renewal, not an instant
“The new man, who is being renewed
in knowledge” Colossians 3:10
Cloth is dipped and dried again and again
Research: a new habit takes 66 days on average
notes: Read Colossians 3:10; “being renewed” is a present passive participle — continual and ongoing.
Note that our age demands everything “right now”, so we expect one conference to remake us and lose heart when it doesn’t.
Picture: cloth dipped and dried again and again — after thirty times it is blue through and through and won’t wash out.
Data: Lally and colleagues at University College London (2010) — a new habit takes sixty-six days on average, ranging from eighteen to two hundred and fifty-four.
Optionally add Maguire’s 2000 PNAS study of London taxi drivers’ hippocampus.

text: Old self: self-centred; new self: selfless
“It is no longer I who live,
but Christ lives in me” Galatians 2:20
Selflessness isn’t becoming nothing
it is entering the limitless and living it out
notes: Read the full verse, Galatians 2:20 — the clearest declaration of selflessness.
Explain that the essence of the old self is “self”: my opinions, my rights, my face, my credit.
Stress that selflessness isn’t becoming zero; the limited “I” steps aside and the limitless Christ is lived out.
321: rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit, not on the brain and ourselves; rely on the brain and you’ll be troubled, rely on the heart and you’ll be glad.
Note that many people can’t change not because they don’t try hard enough, but because they try too hard, forcing it on their own.

text: 3. Jesus Lived It Before Our Eyes
He lived it before our eyes
He died it before our eyes
“I have given you an example” John 13:15
Example: he got down and showed us
notes: Explain that of thirty-three and a half years only three and a half were public ministry; the rest was eating, living and walking together.
On the last night he tied a towel round his waist and washed feet — including those of the man who would betray him.
Read John 13:15; “example” is hypodeigma, a sample set down below for people to see.
Optionally add 1 Peter 2:21: “example” there is hypogrammos, the copybook children traced.

text: Came for the miracles, left at the hardship
“Many of his disciples went back,
and walked no more with him” John 6:66
Only Spirit and Understanding: short-lived influence
Add Life, and there is a foundation
notes: Read John 6:66; those who wanted to crown him king yesterday turned and left today.
Contrast Peter’s answer (John 6:68): Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
Analyse the difference: those who left came to get something; those who stayed handed over their whole lives.
Conclusion: with only Spirit and Understanding, influence is short-lived; add Life, and there is a foundation.

text: Founded on the rock
“It didn’t fall, for it
was founded on the rock” Matthew 7:25
The rain still falls, the wind still blows
A tree that never faced the wind cannot stand
notes: Read Matthew 7:25; the rain still fell, the floods still came, the wind still blew.
The difference wasn’t the weather but the foundation; everyone meets wind and rain.
Illustration: the trees in Biosphere 2 grew fast but toppled before maturity, because there was no wind in the glasshouse.
Explain that trees buffeted by wind grow stress wood and drive their roots deeper.
Apply: Spirit and Understanding are growing upward; Life is putting down roots; the unseen part decides whether a tree stands.

text: Passing on life by life, life influencing life
“Not the Good News of God only,
but also our own souls”
1 Thessalonians 2:8
What has the most influence is life
notes: Read the full verse, 1 Thessalonians 2:8: not the Good News only, but our own souls as well.
Psychology: Bandura’s social learning theory (1977) and the Bobo doll experiment (1961).
History: Polycarp, martyred around AD 155 — eighty-six years I have served him, and he has never done me wrong.
Optionally add Mackay, who reached Tamsui in 1872 and is believed to have said, “Rather burn out than rust out.”

text: Practices (1)
Choose to act: live out one truth
Examine your life: do inside and outside match?
Keep being renewed: write down one mindset daily

Practice 2, examine your life, matches stage five, Evaluation: three minutes before bed, three questions.

Three Foundations, Two Core Values, the Goal
Spirit → Understanding → Life → Service → God
Life first, then relationships, then ministry
920 practice, 235 relationships
notes: The Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model, the Bible is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide.
The Two Core Values: let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory; the Goal: establish God’s system.

text: Closing: living out Jesus with our lives
Faith is no longer just a mindset
but a life
It isn’t you who influences people
it is Christ influencing people through you
notes: Key point: service that stops at Spirit and Understanding is incomplete; it must enter Life.
Read John 15:5; the branch doesn’t manufacture fruit — it only stays joined to the vine.
Stress: not pushing harder but drawing closer — letting Jesus live a little more.
Call: let Jesus be King — a king is not a consultant; his word is final.
Close with the lesson’s final line: living out Jesus with our lives.

Carry me from knowledge into life
from receiving into living it out
Life influencing life
All glory to the Lord
notes: Lead the brothers and sisters in praying together; slow the pace and leave space for response.
Base the prayer on the lesson’s declaration: from knowledge into life, from receiving into living it out.
Include confession: we often stop at being moved and at knowing, and never step into action.
Declare Galatians 2:20: it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.
