script: Brothers and sisters, good morning. Today we come to Lesson 172 of Morning Devotion 321, the summary of the whole Morning Devotion 321 series, and its title is “Live Out Christ, Become a Victor”. We have two theme verses. The first is Romans 8:37: “No, in all these things, we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.” The second is Revelation 3:21: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame, and sat down with my Father on his throne.” Today’s lesson is like stringing together all the pearls we have gathered along the way into a single necklace.

In the last lesson we learned “Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God”. Today we want to gather the whole of 321 into one direction: live out Christ, become a Victor. Learning 321 is not just about remembering concepts or understanding teaching; it is about letting the truth enter our lives and letting Jesus be King within us. However well a medical student knows his anatomy, only when he cares for patients at the bedside does that knowledge become real power. We hold on to it with three sentences: the Three Foundations direct us to follow the Lord; the Two Core Values help us honour the Lord as King; the Goal leads us to build together with one heart. And there is just one key: turning from the self-centred life to selflessness. Brothers and sisters, if 321 stays in our notebooks, it is merely an attractive framework; only when it walks into our daily lives does it become life.

Selflessness does not mean denying our own worth, nor abandoning our responsibilities; it means no longer putting ourselves at the centre, and willingly letting Jesus rule. And victory doesn’t mean green lights all the way from now on. True victory is to keep trusting the Lord in difficulty, to keep obeying the Lord in temptation, and to keep living out the Lord’s love in our relationships. Our circumstances may not have changed yet, but our lives have already begun to change. Because the foundation of our victory is not in ourselves, but in the Lord Jesus, who loved us, gave himself up for us, and has already risen victorious.

When Paul wrote Romans 8, he listed oppression, anguish, persecution and the sword. Within ten years, the believers in Rome really did face Nero’s persecution. And right there, Paul says “more than conquerors” — in the original, hypernikaō, a victory that goes far beyond. Revelation 3:21 was written to Laodicea. That was a wealthy city that rebuilt itself by its own resources after an earthquake, and the church said too, “I am rich, and have need of nothing” — and ended up lukewarm. Yet the Lord stood at the door and knocked, and even gave them his highest promise. From knocking outside the door, to dining together, to sitting together on the throne: this is the road of victory, turning from the self-centred life to selflessness.

The starting point of victory is “through him who loved us”. It is not that we become perfect first and then the Lord accepts us; while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. So first of all we must stand firm on the Three Foundations: Jesus is my role model, the Bible is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide. From “what I think” to “what the Lord says”. The Lord Jesus said, “I have overcome the world.” We are not fighting for an uncertain victory; we are walking into a victory the Lord has already won. Victory doesn’t suddenly happen when the storm comes; it is decided on the ordinary days when we build our house on the rock.

Next come the Two Core Values: let Jesus be King, and let Jesus receive all the glory. Our problem is often that the “I” within us wants to be in control. Many quarrels are really about who gets the final say. Humility means letting humans be human and letting God be God. We are the branches, he is the vine; apart from him we can do nothing. The elders in heaven all lay their crowns before the throne. The lordship goes to Jesus, and the glory goes to Jesus as well.

Paul says, “It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.” Living out Christ means a little more understanding at home, a little more gentleness in conflict. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your living changes. Every day, in our seeing, listening, thinking, speaking and doing, we choose again and again to deny ourselves. See: don’t rush to find fault. Listen: don’t rush to contradict. Think: consider the Lord’s heart. Speak: say words that build others up. Do: take action in love.

This is 920. A family member says something hurtful, the anger rises — stop for a moment and pray: “Lord, please rule my heart, and rule my mouth too.” Overcoming anger is victory; being willing to apologise is victory; letting go of revenge is victory. When we fail, we come straight back to the Lord, confess, and stand up again. But denying self is not giving way without limits, either; it includes facing problems honestly and setting appropriate boundaries. For a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again.

The Goal of 321 is to establish God’s system. It begins with a group of people who let Jesus be King. The order is: life first, then relationships, then ministry. In 235 we support one another, walk alongside one another in growth and work together as one, and in our serving we walk the road of Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God every day. We follow the Lord ourselves, and we walk alongside others as they follow him too. People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. In the second century Polycarp said that he had served the Lord for eighty-six years, and the Lord had never done him wrong. That is a Victor who was faithful to the end.

To sum up 321: the Three Foundations give our life roots; the Two Core Values give our life a Lord; the Goal has us building together with one heart. Our focus is Jesus; we rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit. The foundation of victory is in Christ, the strength comes from the Lord, and the glory goes to God. 321 is not about making us a more impressive version of ourselves, but about making us people who are more like Jesus.

So, five things every day: stand firm on the Three Foundations; hold fast to the Two Core Values; practise 920 once; live in the order of life, relationships, ministry; and follow faithfully with eternal hope. In the evening, look back: where you have failed, confess; where you have received something, put it into practice. Don’t give up following because of one failure, and don’t stop relying on him because things are going well for a while. Through him who loved us, we can still stand today, and we will keep following tomorrow.

Brothers and sisters, the Lord is still standing at the door and knocking today. Let us open the door to him and let him be King. Let us pray together: Lord Jesus, thank you for loving us first. We hand the lordship over to you; please be King in our families, our relationships and our serving, so that we live out Christ and are faithful to the end, until we sit with you on your throne. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, Amen. Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.

Brothers and sisters, good morning. Today we come to Lesson 172 of Morning Devotion 321, the summary of the whole Morning Devotion 321 series, and its title is “Live Out Christ, Become a Victor”. We have two theme verses: Romans 8:37, “No, in all these things, we are more than conquerors through him who loved us,” and Revelation 3:21, “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame, and sat down with my Father on his throne.” Today, let us take hold once more, in full, of the whole of the 321 we have walked through together.

In the last lesson we learned “Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God”: beginning with the guidance of the Holy Spirit, renewing our mindset through the truth, following Jesus’ example to live out his life, letting Jesus be King in our serving, and finally giving the glory to God. Today we want to gather all the 321 we have learned into one direction: live out Christ, become a Victor. Brothers and sisters, learning 321 is not just about remembering concepts, nor just about understanding teaching. A medical student may know his anatomy inside out, and still not be a doctor; only when he cares for patients at the bedside, time after time, does his knowledge become real power. 321 is the same: only when it walks into our homes, our workplaces and our churches does it become life. Over these days we have read many lessons and noted quite a few terms: the Three Foundations, the Two Core Values, the Goal, 920, 235, the eight stages. The question today is not how much we have remembered, but how much we have lived out.

We can hold on to this road with three sentences: the Three Foundations direct us to follow the Lord; the Two Core Values help us honour the Lord as King; the Goal leads us to build together with one heart. And the key to everything is turning from the self-centred life to selflessness. Selflessness does not mean denying our own worth, nor abandoning our responsibilities; it means no longer putting ourselves at the centre. And victory doesn’t mean green lights all the way from now on. True victory is to keep trusting the Lord in difficulty, to keep obeying the Lord in temptation, and to keep living out the Lord’s love in our relationships. Our circumstances may not have changed yet, but our lives have already begun to change. And remember: the foundation of our victory is not in ourselves, but in the Lord Jesus, who loved us, gave himself up for us, and has already risen victorious.

First, let’s look at Romans. Paul wrote this letter around AD 56 to 57. Chapter 7 ends with a cry: “What a wretched man I am!” And at the very start of chapter 8 the dawn breaks: “There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.” In the second half, Paul asks: who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Oppression? Persecution? The sword? Within ten years, Nero’s persecution really did fall on the believers in Rome. And right there, Paul says “more than conquerors” — in the original, hypernikaō, a word that appears only once in the New Testament, meaning a victory that goes far beyond. Paul goes on to say he is persuaded that neither death nor life, neither things present nor things to come, nor any other created thing can separate us from God’s love in Christ.

Now let’s look at Revelation. It was written by the apostle John on the island of Patmos, and chapter 3 contains the letter to the church in Laodicea. Laodicea was very rich: a financial centre with a medical school. After a great earthquake, it declined Roman aid and rebuilt itself by its own means. Its water was piped in from outside and arrived lukewarm. So the Lord says, “You are neither cold nor hot.” The church said, “I am rich, and have need of nothing.” That is the self-centred life. Yet the Lord did not give up on them. He stood at the door and knocked, and he gave this very church the highest promise in all seven letters. From knocking outside the door, to dining together, to sitting together on the throne: this is the road walked by those who turn from the self-centred life to selflessness.

The starting point of our victory is “through him who loved us”. It is not that we first become perfect and then the Lord accepts us; rather, “while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.” Jesus said, “In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.” Brothers and sisters — “I have overcome”: we are not fighting for an uncertain victory; we are walking into a victory the Lord has already won. And John says: “This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith.”

So we must stand firm on the Three Foundations. Jesus is my role model: when something happens, learn his humility, obedience, holiness and kindness. The Bible is my standard: don’t let trends or our own preferences be the highest standard; let God’s word correct us. The Holy Spirit is my guide: seek him in prayer, keep an obedient heart — and the Holy Spirit’s guidance will never contradict the Bible. These Three Foundations help us turn from “what I think” to “what the Lord says”. Victory doesn’t happen only when the storm comes; it is decided on the ordinary days when we build our house on the rock.

Next come the Two Core Values. First, let Jesus be King. Our problem is often not just that something has been done wrongly, but that the “I” within us wants to be in control. Many quarrels are really about who gets the final say. How to wash the dishes, how to park the car — it’s no big deal, but as soon as it touches “I want to be in charge”, the temper flares. So victory begins with letting go: letting go of our insistence on being in charge, returning to our originally intended position as created beings, and handing the lordship over to Jesus. When Laodicea said “I have need of nothing”, that was exactly the heart that wants to be in charge of itself.

Humility means letting humans be human and letting God be God. The Lord said, “I am the vine. You are the branches.” A cut branch, however sturdy, withers within a few days. We need to stay joined to the Lord every day. The second core value is to let Jesus receive all the glory. The elders in heaven lay their crowns before the throne. A Victor is not someone who clutches the crown, but someone who offers the crown to the Lord. The Three Foundations give our life roots; the Two Core Values give our life a Lord.

Once the foundation is firm, we must live it out. Paul says, “It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.” And then he adds: “who loved me, and gave himself up for me.” We can deny ourselves because he first gave himself up for us. Living out Christ is not just being devout at meetings; it is a little more understanding at home, a little more gentleness in conflict, staying honest when we are wronged, and building one another up in our serving. How beautifully a person prays from the platform is not the true measure of their spiritual stature; how they speak when they get home — that is.

A change of life begins with our mindset. Romans 12 says, “be transformed by the renewing of your mind” — and “transformed” is the word for a caterpillar becoming a butterfly. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your living changes. From the human point of view to God’s point of view, from the temporary to the eternal. In the past we said, “He has upset me, so I’ll show him what I’m made of.” Now we say, “Lord, help me live out your life in this situation.” It is the same situation and the same person, but the starting point within us is completely different. This is turning from the reactions of the old self to the life of the new self.

How exactly do we practise it? Through See, Listen, Think, Speak, Do. See: don’t rush to find fault; see people’s needs. Listen: don’t rush to contradict; patiently understand the other person. Think: don’t only calculate for yourself; consider the Lord’s heart. Speak: don’t wound carelessly; speak words that build others up. Do: don’t only seek your own convenience; take action in love. The Lord says to take up our cross “daily”; denying self is small choices made again and again, every day. James says: “Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.”

This is 920. The ninefold fruit of the Spirit grows through selflessness before everyone we relate to. A family member says something hurtful, the anger rises — stop for a moment and pray: “Lord, rule my heart, and rule my mouth too.” Then listen well and speak gently. John Gottman, who studies marriage, observed that in stable couples, positive and negative interactions run at about five to one. After the war, Corrie ten Boom held out her hand to a former guard from the concentration camp; it was not that her love was big enough, but that the Lord’s love flowed through her. Overcoming anger, being willing to apologise, letting go of revenge — all of these are victory. The fruit is not something we squeeze out; it is what the Holy Spirit produces in us when we move the self out of the way.

But denying self is not giving way without limits. It also includes facing problems honestly, setting appropriate boundaries, taking responsibility and seeking help. We learn Jesus’ gentleness, and we also learn his faithfulness to the truth. What if we fail? Come straight back to the Lord: confess, repent and receive forgiveness. “For a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again.” Through Information, Revelation, Conviction, Implementation, Evaluation, Correction, Repetition and Multiplication, we let the truth become our way of life.

Back to Revelation 3:21. The Lord gave the promise of sitting with him on his throne to Laodicea, the church that most needed to repent. As long as we open the door, no one is too far from victory. The Lord says, “as I also overcame”. How did Jesus overcome? He emptied himself, took the form of a servant, and was obedient to death. So today we must learn to let him be King: honouring the Lord as great in our choices, learning to love in our relationships, being faithful and responsible in our serving, and keeping the faith in difficulty.

The Goal of 321 is to establish God’s system. It doesn’t begin with an organisation chart, but with a group of people who let Jesus be King. The order is: life first, then relationships, then ministry. People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. When pushing things forward, cherish people; when dealing with problems, have regard for relationships. Many teams fall apart not because there is too little ministry, but because the order has been turned upside down.

On this foundation we develop 235: the 2 is spiritual companions who support one another; the 3 is spiritual parents and children, walking alongside one another in growth; the 5 is a fivefold ministry team, building together with one heart. And in our serving we walk the road of Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God every day. In the second century Polycarp was told to curse Christ, and he said: I have served him for eighty-six years, and he has never done me wrong. That is a Victor who was faithful to the end. This is also the heart of the Lord’s Prayer: let your Kingdom come; let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

The lesson gives us a reminder: the Three Foundations must become what we follow every day, the Two Core Values the choice of our hearts, and the Goal the direction in which we build together. Becoming a Victor is a lifelong journey of relying on the Lord. The foundation of victory is in Christ, the strength for victory comes from the Lord, and the glory of victory goes to God. When we are weak, we can come to the Lord; when we fail, we can repent and stand up again. The Lord’s grace helps us keep going forward.

So here is the whole picture of 321: the Three Foundations, the Two Core Values, the Goal; turning from the self-centred life to selflessness, returning in humility to our originally intended position; the focus is Jesus, relying on the heart and the Holy Spirit; renewing our mindset through the eight stages, living 920 in our relationships, walking together in 235, and serving by Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God. The destination is sitting with the Lord on his throne. 321 is not about making us a more impressive version of ourselves, but about making us people who are more like Jesus.

Five things every day. First, stand firm on the Three Foundations: draw near to the Lord, read the Bible and pray. Second, hold fast to the Two Core Values: hand over to the Lord the thing you most want to control — “Lord Jesus, I hand this matter over to you.” Third, practise 920 once: one less word of rebuke, one more word of encouragement. Fourth, live in the order of life, relationships, ministry: take the initiative to care for a family member or a companion. Fifth, follow faithfully with eternal hope: look back in the evening; where you have failed, confess; where you have received something, put it into practice. Let God’s word set the direction for the day’s living, and let the fruit of the Spirit appear in concrete words and actions. Don’t give up because of one failure, and don’t stop relying on him because things are going well for a while.

Brothers and sisters, as we follow the Lord like this, those who were quick to anger begin to learn gentleness; those who held on tightly begin to be willing to entrust things to him; those who cared only for themselves begin to reach out to others. The Lord is still standing at the door and knocking today; let us open the door to him. Let us pray together: Lord Jesus, thank you for loving us first. We hand the lordship over to you; please be King in our families, our relationships and our serving, so that we live out Christ, walk alongside others on the road of victory, and are faithful to the end, until we sit with you on your throne. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, Amen. Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.
